title: Guy Pearce Reunites With Andrew Baird for Irish Thriller ‘Bottle’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Guy Pearce and filmmaker Andrew Baird will reunite for their fourth film, an upcoming Irish thriller titled “Bottle.”

	The actor will play Jimmy, a
body:
Guy Pearce and filmmaker Andrew Baird will reunite for their fourth film, an upcoming Irish thriller titled “Bottle.”

	The actor will play Jimmy, a historically violent pub owner who traps a troubled young man named Cillian after he breaks into his bar in search of a pint. As Cillian fights to survive the night, he begins to piece together exactly why Jimmy is holding him against his will.


	“‘Bottle’ brought to mind the classic crime films of the ‘70s, such as Peter Yates’ ‘The Friends of Eddie Coyle,’ with a similar DNA to John Hillcoat’s ‘The Proposition,’ which Guy starred in,” Baird said. “What separates this from my previous pictures is that it is inherently Irish and lives in a very dark, traumatic and bruised world, reflecting an old Ireland that I know very well and grew up in. It has never been captured in this way before on film.”
	

	The film will shoot on-site in Ireland with a screenplay by Roberto Forte and Eamonn O’Brien. Marco Gomez serves as executive producer, with FJ Productions’ Fabio Golombek and Shannon Alexander producing alongside Samson Films’ David Collins.


	Pearce previously collaborated with Baird on “Zone 414,” “Sunrise” and “The Marshal,” which is set to release in 2027. The actor most recently starred in Ridley Scott’s “The Dog Stars” alongside Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley and Josh Brolin. The film brought in $8 million domestically during its opening weekend despite costing over $80 million to produce.

	Pearce is repped by Independent Talent Group and Creative Artists Agency. Baird is repped by Source Management + Production.

title: How to Watch ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Online Without Cable
description:
The ballroom is officially back open.

	“Dancing With the Stars” returned this week for its 35th season, kicking off with a two-night premiere on Tu
body:
The ballroom is officially back open.

	“Dancing With the Stars” returned this week for its 35th season, kicking off with a two-night premiere on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and Wednesday, Sept. 16 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+. After the premiere, new episodes will continue airing live Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET. Episodes are also available to stream on Hulu the following day.

	Another convenient way to stream new episodes live is on DirecTV, whose streaming packages carry local ABC stations in most markets. The service, which offers a five-day free trial, also currently bundles Disney+ and Hulu with ads.


	Sling TV, Fubo and Hulu + Live TV also offer ways to watch “Dancing With the Stars” live on ABC without cable. Sling Blue starts at $45.99 per month and includes ABC in select markets, while Fubo carries the network in supported areas through its live TV packages, starting at $73.99 per month. Hulu + Live TV, meanwhile, starts at $89.99 per month and includes ABC alongside more than 100 live channels, plus bundled access to Hulu and Disney+. 

	Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough are back as co-hosts this season, while Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough return to the judges’ table. This year’s celebrity cast includes “Save the Last Dance” star Julia Stiles, “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” alum Tatyana Ali, “Grey’s Anatomy” star Harry Shum Jr., celebrity chef Giada De Laurentiis, “The Bachelorette” alum Tyler Cameron, “Summer House” star Ciara Miller, Olympian Amber Glenn and “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” fixture Guillermo Rodriguez.


	Also competing are Paralympian Ezra Frech, Hanson singer Taylor Hanson, “Love Island U.K.” alum Maura Higgins, “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Conner Leavitt, Savannah Bananas player Jackson Olson, model Sarah Jane Nader and comedian Connor Wood. Among the returning pros are Mark Ballas, Witney Carson, Jenna Johnson, Val Chmerkovskiy, Emma Slater, Rylee Arnold and Daniella Karagach.

title: ‘Yellowstone’ Alum Jefferson White Joins ‘Marshals’ Season 2
description:
Jefferson White is saddling back up as Jimmy Hurdstrom, with the actor set to reprise his “Yellowstone” role in “Marshals” Season 2 at CBS. 

	White
body:
Jefferson White is saddling back up as Jimmy Hurdstrom, with the actor set to reprise his “Yellowstone” role in “Marshals” Season 2 at CBS. 

	White will recur in the second season of the CBS drama, which stars fellow “Yellowstone” alum Luke Grimes as Kayce Dutton. 

	“I’m thrilled to dive into the world of ‘Marshals’ and continue exploring the American West,” White said in a statement. “The cast and crew are stacked full of my favorite actors and filmmakers, and I’m honored to join them. Jimmy and I have been through a lot together, and I can’t wait to see what’s next for us.”
	

	Exactly how Jimmy will be worked into the show remains to be seen. Fans of “Yellowstone” will remember that Jimmy’s storyline concluded with John Dutton giving Jimmy his blessing to return to Texas the 6666 Ranch permanently, where Jimmy builds a life as a cowboy and horse trainer. 


	White is now the latest “Yellowstone” star to appear in “Marshals.” Along with Grimes, the show also features Brecken Merrill (Tate Dutton), Gil Birmingham (Thomas Rainwater), and Mo Brings Plenty (Mo). 

	Along with his time on “Yellowstone,” White is known for his roles in shows like “House of Cards,” “The Alienist,” “The Americans,” and “How to Get Away with Murder.” In film, he has starred in features like “Civil War” and “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” His upcoming credits include “Rambo” with Noah Centineo and “November 1963.” 

	He is repped by Lichter Grossman, Principal Entertainment LA and Gersh.

	In “Marshals,” Kayce Dutton joins a U.S. Marshals unit fighting to deliver justice in Montana. The cast also includes Logan Marshall-Green, Arielle Kebbel, Ash Santos, and Tatanka Means. 
	

	The series was renewed for a second season less than two weeks after it premiered earlier this year. It is set to premiere Oct. 4 on CBS and streaming the next day on Paramount+. 

	“Marshals” was developed by Spencer Hudnut, based on characters created by Taylor Sheridan and John Linson. Hudnut also serves as showrunner and executive producer. Sheridan executive produces along with David Glasser, John Linson, Art Linson, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, Michael Freidman, Grimes, and Keith Cox. It is produced by Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios.

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Adds Six to Cast, Including ‘Letterkenny’ Alum Michelle Mylett, Lauren Chan
description:
“Heated Rivalry” Season 2 is continuing to build out its cast with the addition of six new actors. 

	The highly-anticipated second season of the Cr
body:
“Heated Rivalry” Season 2 is continuing to build out its cast with the addition of six new actors. 

	The highly-anticipated second season of the Crave-HBO Max series has added: Brendan Morgan (“F*** Marry Kill,” “The Handmaid’s Tale”) as Zane Boodram, David Tomlinson (“Fellow Travelers,” “Silent Night”) as Cody Kent (Dallas Kent in the books), Gerry Dee (“Mr. D,” “Animal Control”) as Coach Cooper, Michelle Mylett (“Letterkenny,” “El Camino Christmas”) as Lisa, Lauren Chan (“The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Canada’s Drag Race”) as Gen, and Nick Stahl (“Let the Right One In,” “Terminator 3″) as Curtis Barrett.
	

	The castings reunite “Heated Rivalry” creator Jacob Tierney with Dee, Mylett, and Stahl. Tierney previously directed Dee in the CBC sitcom “Mr. D,” while he and Mylett co-starred in the popular Crave series “Letterkenny,” which Tierney also co-created, directed, and executive produced. Stahl starred in the 2003 movie “Twist,” which was written and directed by Tierney. 


	Morgan is repped by The ART Agency and Thruline Entertainment. Tomlinson is repped by Glickman Alexander Talent Management & Play Management. Dee is repped by Connekt Creative. Mylett is repped by The Arthur Agency and Link Entertainment. Chan is repped by P1M, JAG Models, INSURGE-Ent, align PR and Yorn Levine. Stahl is repped by LINK Entertainment, Artium Talent and attorney Blake Zurbuchen.

	The hit series is based on the “Game Changers” books by Rachel Reid. Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie will return in the lead roles. The cast of Season 2 will also include: Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Daniel Diemer, Shaheen Jafargholi, Robert Naylor, Sophie Nélisse, Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova, Edvin Ryding, François Arnaud, Christina Chang, Dylan Walsh, Robbie G.K., Callan Potter, Benjamin Roy, Kamilla Kowal, Emily Hampshire, Sabrina Jalees, Priyanka, Kevin Zegers, Paul Gross and Milla Jovovich.
	

	Season 2 will premiere in the spring of 2027 on HBO Max. The official logline for Season 1 states, “Rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) are bound by ambition, rivalry, and a magnetic pull neither of them fully understood. What began as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies evolved into a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery.”

	The series is commissioned by Bell Media’s Crave with the participation of the Canada Media Fund (CMF). Tierney serves as writer, director, and executive producer. Brendan Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson also executive produce. Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje are producers, with Reid as consulting producer. Mike Goldbach serves as co-writer on Season 2. The series is distributed internationally by Sphere Abacus, a Bell Media company. The series is produced by Accent Aigu Entertainment in association with Crave.

title: Oscars: France Selects Cannes Prizewinner ‘Minotaur’ for International Feature Race
description: France has selected Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur” to represent the country in the international feature film race at the
body:
France has selected Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur” to represent the country in the international feature film race at the Oscars.

	The choice was made Wednesday by France’s Oscar committee following auditions with the producers, international sales agents and U.S. distributors behind the five-shortlisted films, including Mubi, Neon and Sony Pictures Classics.


	“Minotaur” prevailed in a particularly eclectic and wide-open field that also included Antonin Baudry’s two-part historical epic “De Gaulle,” Arthur Harari’s “The Unknown,” Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva” and Louis Clichy’s animated feature “Iron Boy.”
	

	The selection of “Minotaur” reflects France’s growing role as a production and financing hub for filmmakers from outside the country. Last year, France submitted Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi’s “It Was Just an Accident,” which had won the Palme d’Or at Cannes and went on to secure an Oscar nomination. The choice had sparked pushback in parts of the French industry over whether a country should be represented by a foreign-born filmmaker working largely outside the French language.


	A dissident Russian filmmaker who lives in exile in France, Zvyagintsev made his Russian-language drama with France’s Charles Gillibert‘s CG Cinéma and MK Productions. A portrait of corruption in contemporary Russia, “Minotaur” is represented internationally by MK2 Films, while Mubi has acquired North America and several other territories.

	“In what promises to be a highly competitive field, this selection underscores both France’s unique role in major global co-productions and our country’s commitment to supporting the great filmmakers of our time, while maximizing our chances of winning the Oscar for Best International Feature Film,” said Gaetan Bruel, the president of the National Film Board (CNC).
	

	“It all starts now. The CNC and Unifrance, determined to ensure that France shines once again this year at this major international film event, will strongly support not only the French nominee but also all French films nominated in any Oscar category, as part of a renewed strategy. The goal is to win,”  he continued. 

	The country has not won the international feature prize since Régis Wargnier’s “Indochine” took the honor in 1993, despite remaining one of the category’s most consistently represented nations.

	This year’s French Oscar committee was presided over by Charles Tesson and included Coralie Fargeat, Emilie Lesclaux, Sophie Mas, Grégory Chambet, Nadim Cheikhrouha, Thierry de Clermont-Tonnerre, Ron Dyens, Nicolas Eschbach, Adeline Monzier and Sylvie Pialat.

	The 2027 race also marks the first year under new Academy rules allowing non-English-language films that win the top prize at one of six designated international festivals — Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto and Venice — to enter the international feature race without being their country’s official submission.

	The Academy is set to unveil its 15-film international feature shortlist on Dec. 15, with nominations announced Jan. 21. The 99th Academy Awards will take place March 14, 2027.

schema.headline: Oscars: France Selects Cannes Prizewinner ‘Minotaur’ for International Feature Race

title: ‘Go Vacation on Location’ with Hollywood Location Managers in New Expedia Video Series (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The Los Angeles Tourism & Convention Board is launching a new movie-tourism video series, “Go Vacation on Location” in partnership with Expedia to s
body:
The Los Angeles Tourism & Convention Board is launching a new movie-tourism video series, “Go Vacation on Location” in partnership with Expedia to spotlight the city’s most visitor-friendly filming locations.

	Hosted by real Hollywood location managers, the videos will show tourists and film fans around Los Angeles.

	“Location scouts and managers are among the most important members of our industry’s creative teams and our communities’ best storytellers,” said writer and co-producer Harry Medved. “It’s a pleasure to help L.A. Tourism shine a spotlight on our unsung local heroes, bring them in front of the cameras and highlight their outstanding work in keeping production at home.”
	

	The series will kick off with videos hosted by “La La Land” and “Jumanji: Open World” location manager Tristan Daoussis as he leads viewers around a downtown Los Angeles movie tour anchored by the historic Millennium Biltmore Hotel. Kelly Harris (location manager of “Bel-Air” and “Melrose Place”) will show fans L.A.’s beaches on film, centered around the Venice boardwalk. Scott Trimble (location manager of “Transformers” and “Star Trek”) will explore the San Fernando Valley on film, starting at the Valley Relics Museum.


	“Los Angeles is the original set-jetting destination, with an unparalleled connection to the films and television shows that inspire travel around the world,” Eileen Hanson, chief marketing officer at L.A. Tourism, said. “We’re excited to tap into this growing trend by giving visitors a deeper, more authentic way to explore our city through the locations they have fallen in love with on screen. By partnering with the professionals who help bring these stories to life, we’re not only encouraging visitation to Los Angeles but also championing an industry that supports thousands of local jobs and remains central to our city’s economy and identity.”
	

	Expedia is the official “set-jetting” travel booking partner. L.A. Tourism partnered with members of the Location Managers Guild International as hosts to show viewers locales made famous by productions shot here.

	The videos are produced by Black Buddha Media Group, led by production head Herbie Wei and written and co-produced by Medved and Harry Pallenberg, creators of PBS SoCal’s Emmy-nominated “Locationland” series.

title: Lionsgate, Neon, FilmNation Commit to Career Producer Asks for Healthcare and Development Fees (EXCLUSIVE)
description: A trio of top content makers — Lionsgate Motion Picture Group, Neon and premium independent production house FilmNation — have agreed to new policie
body:
A trio of top content makers — Lionsgate Motion Picture Group, Neon and premium independent production house FilmNation — have agreed to new policies that support Hollywood’s career producers.

	The companies will now provide healthcare protection and upfront development fees for producers, asks made by the collective Producers United — a trade group of over 300 power players who advocate for the rights of those who find material, supervise production and deliver films and TV shows to distributors.
	

	FilmNation, Oscar-heavy Neon and Lionsgate Motion Picture Group (Hollywood’s largest independent studio) join a slew of major companies to support basic rights requests from Producers United, including: Warner Bros. Discovery, Disney, Paramount, Universal and Netflix. The group was formed to combat the “systemic degradation” of the producer’s role in show business, per PU. In a November 2025 Variety cover story, the producers detailed bad practices like “credit proliferation,” where nonproducing talent and financiers take full producer credits and raid fees with no merit. Profit participation for producers has also eroded in the era of streaming.


	There are now four major companies that have not complied with the producer asks: Amazon MGM, Apple, Sony Pictures Entertainment and A24. Last year, Sony insiders told Variety that the studio evaluates healthcare costs according to each individual project. One source familiar with A24 said the company has provisions in place to address producer needs. None of those four companies provided comment for this story.
	

	Lionsgate Motion Picture Group, Neon and FilmNation will cover healthcare by paying into the MPI Non-Affiliate Agreement for a period prior to principal photography, during shooting and for select weeks of postproduction. Producers can alternatively elect to receive an equivalent reimbursement for other health insurance policies that they require, maintain or prefer.

	Development fees, which PU calls “commencement wages,” is a fixed payment producers receive to begin work on a project. The fee, said to be around $25,000, was established in the early ’70s. It has never been adjusted for inflation and is said by producers to be difficult to extract from studios and streamers. The companies will now pay this fee in various tiers at multiples of the standard $25,000, covering stages of script completion and other progress markers.

	“Today’s announcement demonstrates that this is no longer an isolated effort — it is becoming an industry movement,” said the membership of Producers United. “We are grateful to the individual leadership teams of Lionsgate’s Motion Picture Group, Neon and FilmNation for recognizing the importance of creating sustainable careers for producers and for joining the growing number of companies taking concrete action … these commitments acknowledge that career producers are foundational creative and business partners whose work begins years before cameras roll and continues long after production wraps.”

	PU is also actively working to enhance state tax incentives, establish a federal tax incentive, define and implement AI guardrails.

	“We remain committed to working constructively with companies across the industry,” the membership added. “The progress achieved to date demonstrates that thoughtful collaboration can produce meaningful change, and we look forward to continuing these conversations with additional partners in the months ahead.”

schema.headline: Lionsgate, Neon, FilmNation Commit to Career Producer Asks for Healthcare and Development Fees (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Naomi Watts, Demi Moore, Rachel Zegler and More Were Buzzing at Thom Browne’s Bug-Filled NYFW Show
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	The Shed
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	The Shed was abuzz Wednesday night for Thom Browne‘s Spring/Summer 2027 fashion show, which transformed the Hudson Yards arts venue into a lush garden for the finale of New York Fashion Week.

	Luckily for Browne, his A-list front row — Rachel Zegler, Demi Moore, Adam Scott, Britt Lower, Penn Badgley, Anna Wintour, Naomi Watts and Liev Schreiber (the latter two reunited to watch their daughter Kai walk the runway) — are, apparently, big fans of bugs. For his latest offering, the New York designer continued his fascination with creepy-crawlies, sending sequin fly and moth appliqués, butterfly-wing embroidery, jacquard grasshoppers, grass-like tweeds and countless beetles down a circular path surrounding a looming chrysalis. 
	

	At the center of the set sat a giant white cocoon, surrounded by dancers dressed as butterflies, from which a black widow eventually emerged in a black silk duchess gown. The show opened to music from “A Bug’s Life,” while the ambient hum of buzzing bees drifted through much of the presentation.


	Zegler, whose favorite insect is the bee, says the collection was practically made for her. “They’re so smart!” she mused to Variety after the show. “I actually kept bees with my friend Andrew in Ireland. I got stung on the shoulder and it was the best moment ever.”

	The “Evita” star even has matching insect tattoos with her best friends: Zegler has a bumblebee inked on her ribcage, while her two friends have a dragonfly and ladybug, respectively.



	

					Rachel Zegler at the Thom Browne fashion show 
									WWD via Getty Images
	





	

					Janelle Monae at the Thom Browne fashion show
									WWD via Getty Images
	



	Janelle Monáe, meanwhile, gravitated toward the show’s many butterflies. Among the dancers — outfitted in low-slung skirts and high-neck one-piece swimsuits — were, according to the show notes, the “leopard lacewing, the emerald swallowtail, the Arizona hairstreak, the purple emperor, the scarlet Mormon, the Rajah Brooke’s birdwing, the Rothschild’s birdwing, the Apollo, the Sapho longwing, the painted lady.”
	

	“I’m going through my own metamorphosis,” Monáe says of her affinity for the winged creatures.

	Metamorphosis was a fitting theme for Browne himself, whose work has evolved considerably from the appointment-only gray suits he sold out of the West Village at the beginning of his career. He ushered in this brighter, more whimsical chapter in Milan earlier this year, where seersucker flowers, ants, dragonflies, grasshoppers and bee motifs similarly crawled across the collection.



	

					Adam Scott, Britt Lower and Victoria Pedretti at the Thom Browne fashion show 
									WWD via Getty Images
	





	

					Model on the runway at the Thom Browne fashion show 
									WWD via Getty Images
	



	Browne, of course, hasn’t strayed far from his signature tailoring. Amid beekeeper-style hats and beetle-shaped attachés, structured wool coats, tiered pleated skirts and waist-cinching corsets made their way across the Astroturf runway. And at the Emmys the previous night, Browne dressed one of the ceremony’s biggest winners, Matthew Rhys, in a custom three-piece gray tuxedo — quintessential TB.

	But is this especially playful era — even by Browne standards — a final form for the designer? Those who have found the past few years’ red carpets a snooze, should sure hope so. I, for one, would happily welcome a bulbous ladybug or cricket-like exoskeleton at my next premiere.

	I look forward to Zegler getting her hands on one of the collection’s bright yellow apian looks. As she tells Variety: “Thom, if you’re out there: All the bumble bee stuff, you know where to find me!”

title: VidCon Is Leaving Anaheim After Creator Convention Combines With LIONS, Parent of Cannes Lions
description:
VidCon‘s flagship event for digital creators and their fans is leaving its Anaheim home after 16 years in Southern California.

	LIONS, the company
body:
VidCon‘s flagship event for digital creators and their fans is leaving its Anaheim home after 16 years in Southern California.

	LIONS, the company that produces the Cannes Lions advertising and marketing festival in France, announced that it is merging VidCon with its creator-focused events in North America to create VidCon x LIONS Creators. Both LIONS and VidCon are owned by U.K.-based Informa PLC, an international events, digital services and academic research firm.
	

	The primary home of VidCon x LIONS Creators will be the Insight to Impact Festival, LIONS’ North American platform. Insight to Impact debuts in Denver in October 2026 before moving to Nashville in 2027, where the first VidCon x LIONS Creators event will be held. VidCon x LIONS Creators will also have a presence at Cannes Lions in June 2027, with further programming details to be announced.


	VidCon was founded by brothers John and Hank Green in 2010. It was acquired by Viacom in 2018. Paramount Global, Viacom’s successor company, sold VidCon in September 2024 to Informa.

	LIONS’ Insight to Impact Festival brings together Informa’s TMRE: The Market Research Event and Content Marketing World (and VidCon starting next year) along with expertise from across LIONS, including WARC, Contagious and Effie. The platform “will connect consumer understanding, marketing effectiveness and creativity for the North American market,” LIONS said in announcing the change. 

	For the past three years, LIONS has run LIONS Creators, a program dedicated to the intersection of digital influencers and the creative marketing industry. Now, by bringing VidCon into LIONS, “the platform will guide the rapidly growing creator community through its next phase of growth, connecting the ecosystem, and helping brands and creators transform cultural influence into commercial results,” the company said.
	

	LIONS said the move to merge VidCon into its North America business is part of a wider move by the company to evolve its global model across North America, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East and North Africa to be more accessible year-round.

	“The creator economy has never moved faster or mattered more within the global marketing ecosystem,” LIONS CEO Simon Cook said in a statement. “Creators are increasingly central to how culture is created and how brands connect with audiences. The introduction of VidCon is an exciting next step which will allow us to build out a dedicated global platform for an industry that’s rapidly reshaping the marketing landscape.”

	Sarah Tortoreti, VP and business lead at VidCon, said: “For 15 years, VidCon has been the heartbeat of the creator community — the place where emerging and established creators, fans, brands, and industry leaders come together to celebrate digital culture in real life. Joining LIONS allows us to amplify that mission on a global scale. By combining VidCon’s deep-rooted relationships across the creator economy with LIONS’ unparalleled industry authority and global reach, we’re creating unprecedented opportunities for creators to build their careers, for brands to forge authentic partnerships, and for the entire ecosystem to shape what’s next together.”

	LIONS said Cannes Lions, a global festival celebrating creativity, “will remain the centre of the LIONS ecosystem.” Regional platforms will “complement Cannes Lions by making more of LIONS’ expertise accessible throughout the year, while creating stronger connections between local communities and the global stage,” according to the company.

	LIONS is making changes in APAC and MENA regions too: 


Spikes Asia, after almost four decades, will become LIONS Asia in September 2027, in continued partnership with Haymarket Asia. The event, featuring the Asia Lions Awards, will combine Spikes Asia’s regional heritage with LIONS “intelligence, learning and community programs,” according to the company. Programming will be developed with “communities across the region, ensuring Asia-Pacific’s distinct perspectives and innovations help shape the global conversation on creative marketing excellence,” LIONS said.
In December 2027, LIONS Riyadh will be introduced in partnership with Tahaluf — a joint venture among Informa PLC, the Saudi Federation For Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) and the Saudi Events Investment Fund (EIF) — and Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Media. LIONS Riyadh will serve the local creative and marketing community by providing access to global benchmarks, intelligence, and learning, while creating opportunities for local talent and work to connect with the wider international industry. The platform is intended to include a strategic alliance with Athar, run by LIONS’ partner Motivate Media Group, complementing the established Dubai Lynx partnership across the region.



	RELATED: Cannes Lions 2026: The Pitches, Panels, Parties and Prognostication That Resonated Most During a Scorching Week on the Croisette

title: How American High Scored Big With ‘Minimum Wage’ Netflix Series While Building a Pipeline for the Next Generation of Comedians (EXCLUSIVE)
description: It all started with Jeremy Garelick’s simple but ambitious plan for American High: Buy a high school in upstate New York and turn it into the hottes
body:
It all started with Jeremy Garelick’s simple but ambitious plan for American High: Buy a high school in upstate New York and turn it into the hottest filming spot in town for coming-of-age comedies.

	Since the full-scale production outfit was founded in 2017 and American High Shorts launched online in 2022, Garelick’s motto for discovering talent has been to put the funniest people in a room together and let them prove themselves — whether that be in one of their films that end up streaming on Hulu, or a short-form comedy sketch.
	

	Now, that motto is taking the young talent discovered through American High farther than they ever could have imagined with the 28-episode Netflix order for “Minimum Wage” (as Variety exclusively reported in April). It started out as a web series posted on YouTube back in May 2024 made for under $2,000, but Variety can exclusively reveal that the first 14 episodes of “Minimum Wage” will premiere on Netflix on Oct. 26. 


	“It’s the same philosophy we have with film, but in the digital space. If someone’s doing something cool, we’ll just amplify it without all the gatekeeping,” American High president Will Phelps says. “It’s the model that other people were too afraid to do. And now turn the page, everyone wants to give those creators $10 million to make the next ‘Obsession.’ I think we were probably just there five years earlier.”

	“Unlike all the studios and giant companies that like to just be reactive and see what’s working, they don’t want to take chances on first-time directors or actors,” Garelick adds, with a majority of American High’s films being helmed by first-time directors (including Jillian Bell and Jason Orley).
	

	Working with Netflix was a natural fit for Garelick, who directed the 2023 Adam Sandler movie “Murder Mystery 2” and the show “Best Worst Weekend Ever” for the streamer. “This is the biggest opportunity we’ve had at American High in terms of getting our stuff to the broadest audience,” he says.

	While Garelick and Phelps served as showrunners on “Minimum Wage,” the ethos of collaboration remained largely the same: Cast members had the opportunity to write and direct many of their own episodes.

	When the series was picked up by Netflix, there was, of course, the pressure that came with working with a larger budget and wanting to live up to the original series for a wider audience. But cast member Grace Reiter explains that the show was a natural extension of everything American High has spent years building on its digital platforms.

	“What an amazing first experience in a writers’ room and directing your friends. We already built such a language working with each other, it’s like second nature,” Reiter says. “It felt totally comfortable to pitch things in the room and to say not funny things and to get ideas turned down.”

	Getting to direct episodes of their own also proved to be a great learning experience for the cast. Reiter says: “It was just maybe coordinating camera movements a little bit more because now we have two cameras. We were more used to, obviously, the vertical frame and cross-shooting, but we tried to carry over all the things that made our digital sketches and web series popular.”

	The original “Minimum Wage” series took the model of the classic workplace comedy, following a group of overworked teenagers trying (and often failing!) to run a pizza shop. The cast included Reiter, Aidan Micho, Hyde Healy, Julia Dicesare, Luke Burke, Ryan Micho and Tommy Armstrong, who all returned for the Netflix series.

	“It was very scrappy, very homemade,” Reiter says of the original web series.

	For Garelick and Phelps, “Minimum Wage” is just one example of how they view all their sketches as possible IP to pitch to streamers. American High has the benefit of its own built-in audience online, with the American High Shorts TikTok account currently holding 2.6 million followers and a collective 248 million likes (and counting) across all videos.
	

	American High’s head of digital, Tristan Hall, who oversees all of the company’s social accounts and marketing efforts for their films, says that the online sketch videos “operate like a Gen Z version of ‘SNL.'” A typical week starts off with a brainstorming session on Monday, a writers’ room on Tuesday, and then production on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

	“The nice thing about social media is you do get that instant verification,” Hall says. “Within 24 hours, we’ll know if the idea is something we want to revisit.”

	American High has focused on organic social media engagement over traditional advertising.  After premiering at SXSW in March, “Pizza Movie” — led by “Stranger Things” star Gaten Matarazzo — was released on Hulu in April, and became one of the company’s buzziest titles online.



	

					“Pizza Movie,” starring Gaten Matarazzo
									Courtesy of American High
	



	“Whatever studio that we’re releasing with will often assist with more traditional marketing, and then we cover the social media side of things,” says Surina Belk-Gupta, American High’s social media manager. “‘Pizza Movie’ was a game changer for us in how we can use our company brand in film marketing.”

	Jon Hurwitz worked alongside American High as a producing partner on the 2021 high school comedy “Plan B” after being attracted by the resource facilities of the company’s Syracuse hub.

	“What struck me was the youth, which is wonderful,” Hurwitz says of his time on set. “A bunch of young people who were passionate and hardworking, getting experience in the film business.”

	The Academy at American High program was established in 2018, giving film students from schools like Syracuse University, Ithaca College and Onondaga Community College the opportunity to intern and work on sets. Now, Garelick estimates that more than 1,500 students apply for internships each semester.

	American High likes to keep folks around. Matt Sacca, who started off as Garelick’s first intern, worked his way up to head of development and is now writing a comedy titled “Second First Date” for the company. Phelps started out as Garelick’s assistant back in 2014, and Hall began as a creative intern back in 2022.

	Filmmakers and producers who have developed a close relationship with Garelick over the years, from his work on films like “The Hangover” and “The Wedding Ringer,” recognize and trust the next generation of comedians he’s bringing up.
	

	Hurwitz says: “We’re working on the latest ‘Harold and Kumar’ movie and there are going to be some young characters in that. Jeremy’s going to be one of my calls where I’ll have him read the script and say, ‘Hey, are there people in your ecosystem that you think would be great?'”

	In addition to the highly anticipated release of “Minimum Wage” later this year, American High is betting big on its first theatrical release, “Rolling Loud,” which stars Owen Wilson and Matt Rife. It was written and written by Garelick and will be released on Oct. 2 from distributor Ketchup Entertainment.

	“We’re going to always write and make the funniest movies that we believe deserve a theatrical release. We just did ‘Pizza Movie’ that I am 1000% certain would’ve crushed in the theater just because I’ve sat through several screenings,” Garelick says, referencing American High’s first-look deal with Hulu that limits films to streaming.

	“It’s just a matter of when distributors realize that comedies do actually work [in theaters] if they’re funny,” he adds.

	“Rolling Loud,” which follows a father and son attending a hip-hop festival in Miami, is also the rare American High production to be shot outside of Syracuse. The only soundstage in the area that would have been big enough to fit a stage the size they needed had been sold off, Garelick says. (They were able to film it in Miami at a Rolling Loud concert.)

	While Garelick says that American High is “open” to continue expanding filming outside of Syracuse, he recognizes the opportunity to continue hiring local crew.

	“It’s just so easy for us to get things up and running — we know every location,” he says. “We can read a script and be like, ‘We’ll shoot that here, this would cost this much.'”

	“Minimum Wage” cast member Burke, who first connected with Garelick after he visited his Syracuse University screenwriting class in 2022 and took a liking to his spec script, was hired as an on-set punch-up writer for “Rolling Loud.”

	“Being on a large feature film set was such an insane learning experience,” Burke says. “It felt like I was part of the process.”

	Members of American High’s sketch comedies are already expanding their footprint onto other shows; Reiter appeared alongside Tim Robinson in his ambitious HBO comedy “The Chair Company,” but she says the set felt just like a scrappy American High shoot.
	

	“The vibes were similar. As a creative, it’s important to surround yourself with people who you trust. It really was just, ‘They’re friends!'” Reiter says. “In between, they were watching audition tapes and then they’d talk about the [basketball] game, sitting there and making each other laugh. And that’s all I’ve ever wished and hoped for — just to make funny things with my friends.”

	As American High gears up for the new school year, a new crop of interns and students interested in working on sets will come across Garelick and Phillips’ desk, becoming part of the ever-growing network.

	“We created an accidental ecosystem that has really helped every aspect of our business. It wasn’t like we were doing this on purpose,” Garelick says. “We were just trying to do what was fun for us.”

schema.headline: How American High Scored Big With ‘Minimum Wage’ Netflix Series While Building a Pipeline for the Next Generation of Comedians (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Travis Kelce Named Victim in Multimillion-Dollar Ponzi Scheme
description:
Travis Kelce
                          Sacked in Multimillion-Dollar Scam
body:
Travis Kelce
                          Sacked in Multimillion-Dollar Scam
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 16, 2026
                            8:19 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 16, 2026
                                11:43 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Travis Kelce knows a thing or two about taking hits ... but prosecutors say the Chiefs superstar got walloped off the field too -- in a massive Ponzi scheme.
      
    
            Kelce was named in federal court Tuesday as one of the people burned by Siddharth Jawahar, who was sentenced to 11 years in prison for a fraud prosecutors say sucked in more than $35 million from investors.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jawahar pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud and was ordered to pay more than $31 million in restitution.
      

            According to the feds, Jawahar ran Swiftarc Capital LLC and funneled nearly all of his clients' money into one investment -- Philip Morris Pakistan.
      
    
            When that bet went south, prosecutors say Jawahar lied to investors about how their money was performing ... while using new investor cash to pay earlier clients.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The feds say he also lived large on the money, splurging on private jets, luxury hotels, restaurants, shopping and pricey apartments.
      
    
            Kelce's exact losses were not disclosed, and prosecutors made clear he was a victim -- not accused of any wrongdoing.
      
    
            His name had previously been linked to a venture fund, though authorities did not spell out exactly how his investment was tied to Jawahar's scheme.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, Kelce's had plenty going on away from football lately ... including marrying Taylor Swift and dropping millions on a lakefront Ohio mansion.
      
    
            Jawahar, meanwhile, will now spend more than a decade behind bars.

title: Lindsay Clancy Hires Karen Read's Attorney to Try and Get Murder Case Dismissed
description:
Lindsay Clancy
                          Taps Karen Read's Attorney to Get Murder Case Tossed
body:
Lindsay Clancy
                          Taps Karen Read's Attorney to Get Murder Case Tossed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 16, 2026
                            9:11 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Lindsay Clancy's bringing in some big guns to try and get her case dismissed ... because it looks like she's tapped Karen Read's lawyer for the job.
      
    
            Attorney Martin Weinberg filed a "notice of limited appearance" with Plymouth Superior Court on Tuesday ... to fight to dismiss her case on the grounds of double jeopardy, The Boston Globe reports.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Weinberg previously argued to have Read's case tossed after her first trial -- for the alleged killing of her boyfriend, John O'Keefe -- ended in a mistrial. The judge shot him down, but Karen was ultimately acquitted.
      

            And as you know, Lindsay's trial also ended in a mistrial ... after an 11-1 hung jury couldn't come to a unanimous verdict on whether she was guilty of murdering her three kids.
      
    
            Both trials played out in Massachusetts.
      
    
            Lindsay's defense lawyer, Kevin Reddington, recently told CBS Mornings that he's planning to file a motion to dismiss, and plans to argue the grounds for double jeopardy on Sept. 29.
      
    
            And based on this new filing ... it seems like Reddington's gonna have some heavy-hitting backup for his day in court.
      
    
            Stay tuned ...

title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce's Building Plans for Ohio Mansion Rejected

Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce
                          Building Plans For $5.35 Million Ohio Mansi
body:
Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce
                          Building Plans For $5.35 Million Ohio Mansion Rejected!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 16, 2026
                            10:48 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Travis Kelce has taken another hit ... this time from a local board that has dragged its heels on greenlighting his and his wife Taylor Swift's proposed new addition to their 21,000-square-foot estate.
      
    
            According to agendas viewed by TMZ ... Travis and Taylor's plan to add a fence to their $5.35 million Ohio mansion, which they purchased back in March, has not been approved yet. Daily Mail was first to report.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The matter -- which was rejected by the local building board -- was brought up before the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board on Aug. 11 and again on Sept. 8 without a resolution.
      

            The problem? Travis and Taylor's plans outline an 8-foot wall ... and according to Bratenahl regulations ... "Solid fences and walls, and fences with less than 75% openness shall not exceed 30 inches in height."
      
    
            We'll see how this local battle plays out since a new plan has been submitted. Meanwhile, this isn't the only frustrating news for Travis.
      
    
            As we reported ... Travis was named in federal court Tuesday as one of the victims of a $35 million Ponzi scheme.
      
    
            While it's been a couple of setbacks for the NFL star ... the Kansas City Chiefs player celebrated their team's first win Monday ... with Tay in attendance.

title: Brazilian Influencer Duda Alves Dead at 22, Cops Investigating as a Suicide
body:
Influencer Duda Alves
                          Dead at 22

            Influencer Duda Alves is dead ... and it sounds like cops suspect she may have died by suicide, TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            Local authorities confirmed the Brazilian content creator died on Sept. 13 ... and the Civil Police of the Federal District told TMZ in a statement that they're investigating her death as a suicide.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            They explained to the outlet that they won't be sharing any more details "in order to protect the privacy of the family."
      

            Alves had amassed over 800,000 followers across her social media platforms ... creating compelling lifestyle content.
      
    
          Waiting for your permission to load TikTok Post.
      
    
            Just days before she died, the influencer posted a video about a breast reduction she'd previously had, explaining "sleazy men" would criticize her for it.
      
    
            She discussed how she opted for the procedure for "comfort" reasons ... as well as "aesthetic" reasons.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Alves had also posted another video ... talking about how she'd been "vomiting a lot and crying from the pain" three weeks post-op.
      
    
            Alves was 22.
